newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Highlands rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Highlands rated a buy.

text.p: Brisbane-based broker Wilson HTM Ltd recommended Highlands Gold Ltd as a buy, reflecting the potential of the group's Papua New Guinea gold prospects.

"We are of the view that none of the upside at Porgera, nor the Frieda project nor the Ramu project are factored into the Highlands' share price yet," Wilson's director of resources research Phil Hutchings said in a research report.
Hutchings said Highlands is currently capitalised at only A$310 million yet the group's 25 percent of gold reserves at the Porgera mine are 2.9 million ounces.

Adjusting for Highlands' debt and cash position meant that Highlands was capitalised at only A$124 an ounce in Porgera reserves, a 40 percent discount on the A$215 an ounce market average for gold stocks currently, Hutchings said.
Porgera also had the potential to lift reserves as well as conduct further underground exploration and improve mill recoveries, Hutchings said.
"Porgera is far from being a mature mine with lots of exploration and the capacity to mitigate the much-feared gold production decline after 2000," he said.
Highlands also intended to develop the high-grade Nena copper-gold deposit in Papua New Guinea and the larger lower-grade Frieda project concurrently, Hutchings said.
This would be a US$1.2 billion to US$1.6 billion project, far out of Highlands' capacity to finance.
"So Highlands is looking for a major company to farm in to fund the feasibility study," he said.
"We believe that Highlands is significantly under-valued and has the potential for a major share price re-rating," he said.
Highlands shares last traded at A$0.56 by 0240 GMT Tuesday.
